subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public `cron run` remain a strictly non-consuming operator/debug action for every cron schedule, with scheduler-owned deletion, counters, backoff, and timing reachable only through internal timer and watcher paths?
rationale: The patch makes a durable user-visible compatibility choice for manual cron execution and persisted scheduler state; source review can assess mechanics, but maintainers must confirm the permanent public contract.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
options.body: Keep public manual runs observational with respect to scheduler state, while internal timer and watcher-terminal execution retain consuming behavior.

options.title: Require explicit destructive execution
options.body: Preserve scheduled state by default but introduce a separately approved explicit operator action for intentionally consuming a one-shot.

options.title: Keep legacy consuming behavior
options.body: Retain manual-run deletion and scheduler mutations, accepting the destructive verification behavior reported by users.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
recommendation.body: Keep public manual runs observational with respect to scheduler state, while internal timer and watcher-terminal execution retain consuming behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged on-exit deletion work defines the adjacent scheduler-consuming contract that this product decision must preserve.
